song.title: Lonely Day
song.tone_character: A thick, saturated Marshall-style distorted tone with plenty of mids, warmer and less sharp than SOAD's earlier albums. A humbucker SG sits in a wide stereo spread with a room-resonance layer, and P-90 doubles thicken it further.

guitar.model: 1962 Gibson SG (main distorted-tone guitar); 1964 Gibson SG Special (P-90) used for doubles
guitar.pickup: Humbucker, bridge pickup most likely for rhythm (PAF-style, model unknown); P-90 on the doubles

amps.channel: Modified high-gain channel (one channel is stock, the other is modded for more gain)

settings.name: Middle
settings.note: guess; the mids are up front

settings.name: Master
settings.note: guess; power tubes being pushed at studio volume

amps.notes: Guitar World confirms this was the main distorted amp for the Mezmerize/Hypnotize sessions; there is no song-specific source for Lonely Day. One forum post claims a Marshall DSL was used, but that is weakly sourced. No settings have been published; all values are guesses.

amps.model: Divided by 13 FTR-37 / W.E.M. Watkins Dominator
amps.notes: Confirmed for the album's clean, harmonized and arpeggio parts (Jazzmaster into the FTR-37, Dominator for drones/arpeggios). No source confirms use on Lonely Day; only relevant if the song has clean layers.

cab.speakers: Probably Celestion G12T-75 or Greenback-style 12-inch speakers (unknown)

mics.position: In the room, picking up the wall of acoustic guitars

cab.notes: Confirmed: one 4x12 cab faced a wall covered floor to ceiling in acoustic guitars, and a room mic recorded those guitars' body resonance. The close-mic model and position are not documented.

pedals.model: None (guitar plugged straight into the amp)
pedals.purpose: Malakian says he uses no compressor and goes straight into the amp; the distortion comes from the amp

original_rig.tuning: Drop C# (C# G# C# F# A# D#)
original_rig.recording_notes: Recorded at Rick Rubin's house in the Hollywood Hills (the 'haunted mansion'). Producers: Rick Rubin and Daron Malakian. Engineer: David Schiffman, with John O'Mahony. Mix: Andy Wallace. Mastering: Vlado Meller. Heavy rhythm parts were often doubled with a humbucker SG plus a P-90 SG Special, and the result was panned wide. The acoustic-guitar wall and room mic added a natural resonance and reverb. Daron played about 90% of the album's bass himself, but Wikipedia credits Shavo for bass on this song. Tuning per Guitar World: the album is in D# with the low string dropped to C#.

factors: slow-tempo power chords and open chord shapes
clean intonation on the bends in the solo

sections.name: Intro / verse
sections.description: Probably the same distorted amp, with softer picking dynamics and more open chords; in places the guitar volume may be backed off a little to clean up the tone. Song-specific information is missing.

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The main tone: full distortion, double-tracked guitars panned wide, possibly with the P-90 SG Special on the doubles. It should sound thicker and wider than the verse.

sections.name: Solo
sections.description: A melodic, singing lead with lots of sustain: the same Marshall distortion with gain up slightly, mids up front, and possibly a light delay or room reverb in the mix. The pickup is unknown (bridge or neck); a mono lead track sitting in the middle is likely.

warnings: No source documents gear specifically for Lonely Day. Everything given is the album-level rig for the Mezmerize/Hypnotize sessions.
Tab sources disagree on the tuning (Drop C, Drop C#, Drop D a half step down, standard). Guitar World says the album is in D# with the low string at C#, and that fits the G# minor key.
BPM estimates range from 75–77 to 113–114 (half time vs. full time); 76 BPM is the counting most sites use. Key is G# minor (Musicnotes gives A minor, probably a transposed arrangement).
A 2025 forum post claims the album was recorded with an SG + RR5 into a Marshall DSL; this conflicts with Guitar World's JMP100 information and is weakly sourced.
No amp settings, mic models or mic positions have been published; those values are guesses.
The arrangement details in the sections (clean layers, solo pickup and effects) are based on listening and inference, not confirmed by a source.
